subject: Power point or similar generation from Shiny via markdown

messages.author: ff699f651734499a
messages.subject: Power point or similar generation from Shiny via markdown
parts:
I have a Shiny application that reads an Excel file that contains many worksheets of genetic information. The user can select the worksheet and then various parameters based on data in the selected sheet. I have provided plots and summary results, everything works fine.

The user would like to generate a set of plots in a power point file(PPT file) with a single plot on each slide based on a series of parameters in shiny. I have tried to generate the PPT file based on markdown and can't get it to function. Should I be able to pass parameters from shiny to markdown? 


I have tried includeMarkdown, htmlOutput , rmarkdown::run . I just can't seem to get this to work. I don't care how long it make take to run as long as it works.. Any reference to a working example would be great.


If there is a question like this I missed it in my searches, I apologize.


Regards,

Richard

messages.author: 45270654016f7b30
messages.subject: Re: Power point or similar generation from Shiny via markdown
parts:
I don't have much time to recreate a minimal example, but I can point you the direction which I have tried.

My personal experience tells me - don't try to use shiny webapp and rmarkdown (includeMarkdown(render("xxx.Rmd"))) for "slides"

You can wrap all your code to fetch data from csv in rmarkdown chunk, use the ioslide format in Rmd, insert your data in chunk for each slide, or use loop to generate slides dynamically.

once that Rmd is completed. just rename it to index.Rmd and drop it to your shiny server folder, shiny server will pick it up and run.
